name: tauri
purpose: The native Windows shell: the WebView2 window, the notification-area icon, starting with Windows, the sidecar lifecycle and the IPC relay to the orchestrator.
rationale: Required by the specification. It uses the system WebView2 instead of bundling Chromium, so the installer stays near 30 MiB, and its capability system lets the WebView reach only the commands BTCortex allows. BTCortex is on 2.12.4; 2.12.5 is a patch release.
windowsNotes: WebView2 Evergreen is installed by the bootstrapper when missing (webviewInstallMode downloadBootstrapper). Tested on Windows 10 22H2 with WebView2 155.

name: tauri-build
purpose: Build script of the shell: embeds the configuration and capabilities and checks the sidecar and resources exist.
rationale: Part of Tauri 2. It also fails the build when a listed resource is missing, which is why the orchestrator build writes openpgp/ and the licence list before every build.

name: @tauri-apps/cli
purpose: Development server and release bundling: NSIS and MSI installers, sidecar placement, resources.
rationale: The supported way to bundle a Tauri 2 application. BTCortex uses a customised NSIS template for a per-user installation without administrator rights.
windowsNotes: NSIS installs per user into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\BTCortex; the MSI needs administrator rights and is built but not tested.

name: tauri-plugin-dialog
purpose: The system open and save dialogs, for PSBT files, exports and backups.
rationale: Files the user picks are read and written by the orchestrator at the chosen path, so the WebView never needs file-system permissions.

name: tauri-plugin-log
purpose: The shell's own log file, rotated and redacted like the orchestrator's.
rationale: Keeps shell and orchestrator diagnostics side by side for Logs & diagnostics.

name: tauri-plugin-notification
purpose: Windows notifications for alerts.
rationale: Alerts such as an unreachable node or an expiring macaroon must be seen when the window is hidden in the notification area.

name: tauri-plugin-opener
purpose: Opens web links in the user's browser.
rationale: Scoped to https:// only, so the WebView cannot ask the system to open anything else. Explorers on the local network that use http:// are opened by the orchestrator from stored addresses instead.

name: tauri-plugin-shell
purpose: Starts and supervises the orchestrator sidecar.
rationale: Used by the shell only: the WebView has no shell permission in its capability, so it cannot start processes.

name: tauri-plugin-single-instance
purpose: One BTCortex per user: a second start focuses the running window.
rationale: Two orchestrators would compete for the same database, nodes and ports.

name: tauri-plugin-window-state
purpose: Remembers the window's size and position.
rationale: Small usability feature with no data of its own.

name: windows
purpose: Win32 bindings for DPAPI (CryptProtectData and CryptUnprotectData) and the registry entry for starting with Windows.
rationale: DPAPI has no Node.js binding, so secrets are protected in the shell with an application entropy and stored by the orchestrator only as protected blobs; the WebView never sees them.
windowsNotes: DPAPI ties secrets to the Windows user; copies of the disk cannot decrypt them, but programs running as the same user can.

name: tokio
purpose: Asynchronous runtime for the shell's sidecar pipes and timers.
rationale: Tauri 2 already runs on tokio; only the sync, time and macros features are enabled.

name: serde
purpose: Serialisation of the IPC messages in the shell.
rationale: The standard Rust serialisation framework, required by Tauri.

name: serde_json
purpose: JSON for the relay between the WebView and the orchestrator.
rationale: The orchestrator speaks JSON-RPC over stdio.

name: thiserror
purpose: Error types in the shell.
rationale: Plain error enums without runtime cost.

name: base64
purpose: Encodes DPAPI blobs for the orchestrator.
rationale: Protected secrets travel to the orchestrator as base64 text.

name: log
purpose: Logging facade in the shell.
rationale: Used with tauri-plugin-log.

windowsNotes: Injecting the application into node.exe invalidates the Node.js Authenticode signature; the sidecar must be signed again for release (see code-signing).
name: Node.js
purpose: The orchestrator runs as a Node.js single executable application (node --build-sea), placed beside the shell as its sidecar.
rationale: One TypeScript code base for the orchestrator with built-in SQLite (node:sqlite), fetch and child processes, and no Node.js installation needed on the user's computer. The executable embeds the Node.js of the machine that builds it: the builds so far used 26.4.0 (2026-06-24), so a release must be built with the newest 26.x to carry its security fixes.

name: esbuild
purpose: Bundles the orchestrator into one CommonJS file for the single executable.
rationale: Fast, deterministic and able to keep OpenPGP.js out of the bundle (a plugin loads it from its own file, for the LGPL).

windowsNotes: Version 155 was present on the test machine; the Evergreen runtime updates itself.
unverifiedClaims: The current Evergreen version number was not looked up; the record names the version seen on the test machine.
name: Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
purpose: Renders the React interface inside the Tauri window.
rationale: The Evergreen runtime ships with Windows 11 and is installed by the bootstrapper on Windows 10, so BTCortex does not bundle a browser engine.

windowsNotes: The MSVC target (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) with the Visual Studio C++ build tools.
unverifiedClaims: 1.99.1 is the toolchain installed on the build machine (rustc -V on 2026-10-23); a newer stable release may exist.
name: Rust toolchain
purpose: Builds the shell (edition 2024, rust-version 1.88 or later).
rationale: Required by Tauri. Release builds use LTO, one codegen unit and stripped symbols.

name: Windows PowerShell 5.1
purpose: Read-only probes the orchestrator runs: listening ports and their programs (Get-NetTCPConnection), disks and volumes, devices (WMI), WSL distributions, the system proxy and metered connections.
rationale: Present on every Windows 10 and 11 installation, without administrator rights. Inputs travel in environment variables, never inside the script text.

name: node:sqlite
purpose: The orchestrator's database: settings, protected secrets, node profiles, jobs, alerts and metrics, with transactional migrations.
rationale: Built into Node.js, so the single executable needs no native add-on for its database.

name: better-sqlite3
purpose: A SQLite binding for Node.js.
rationale: A native add-on built for each Node.js ABI, which a single executable cannot load from inside itself; node:sqlite covers the same need.

name: zeromq
purpose: A ZeroMQ binding for Node.js.
rationale: Another native add-on. Bitcoin Core's notifications need only a ZMTP 3 subscriber with the NULL mechanism, which BTCortex implements in TypeScript over node:net.

unverifiedClaims: The archived state of the repository was not re-checked on 2026-10-23.
name: keytar
purpose: Credential storage through the operating system's keychain.
rationale: A native add-on, and the repository is archived; DPAPI through the shell gives the same protection on Windows without it.

name: Electron
purpose: A desktop shell bundling Chromium and Node.js.
rationale: The specification asks for Tauri and WebView2; Electron would bundle a browser engine of its own and give the renderer process a larger attack surface.

unverifiedClaims: The current Gpg4win version was not looked up for this record.
name: Gpg4win
purpose: GnuPG for Windows, for checking OpenPGP signatures.
rationale: It would have to be installed first and its output parsed; OpenPGP.js checks the signatures inside BTCortex against keys pinned in the application.

name: openpgp
purpose: Checks the OpenPGP signatures on every download against keys pinned in BTCortex.
rationale: Pure JavaScript and strict about key validity at signature time. It is LGPL-3.0-or-later, so it ships as a separate, replaceable file (openpgp/openpgp.cjs) with its licence instead of inside the executable.
windowsNotes: One Bitcoin Core builder signature is reported invalid because OpenPGP.js checks key validity at the signature's creation time; enough others are valid.

name: yauzl
purpose: Reads ZIP archives for the verified installer.
rationale: Streaming and lazy, so every entry's path, type and size can be checked before anything is written.

name: zod
purpose: The shared contracts: every JSON-RPC method's parameters and results, validated on both sides of the boundary, and the shapes of external answers.
rationale: Types and runtime validation from one definition, used by the interface and the orchestrator alike.

name: qrcode
purpose: Makes QR matrices for PSBTs and payment URIs in the orchestrator.
rationale: Pure JavaScript; the interface draws the matrices as SVG paths.

name: @ngraveio/bc-ur
purpose: Uniform Resources (ur:crypto-psbt) with fountain codes, for animated PSBT QR codes.
rationale: The encoding air-gapped signers such as Keystone and Passport read. Last released in 2024-04; stable.

name: typescript
purpose: The language of the interface, the orchestrator and the packages, in strict mode.
rationale: BTCortex stays on 6.0.x: typescript-eslint 8.72.0, which lints the repository, supports TypeScript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, so 7.x waits for typescript-eslint.

name: vitest
purpose: Unit, component and integration tests, in three projects (node, desktop, integration).
rationale: Shares Vite's configuration and TypeScript handling; integration tests run against real regtest services.

name: tsx
purpose: Runs the TypeScript development scripts (scripts/dev/install-*.ts).
rationale: No separate compile step for scripts.

name: eslint
purpose: Linting of the whole repository.
rationale: Flat configuration with typescript-eslint's type-aware rules.

name: typescript-eslint
purpose: Type-aware lint rules.
rationale: Catches unsafe any, floating promises and unnecessary conditions.

name: @eslint/js
purpose: ESLint's recommended rules.
rationale: Baseline rule set.

name: globals
purpose: Global variable sets for ESLint.
rationale: Node and browser globals per file group.

name: prettier
purpose: Formatting, checked in CI-style runs (npm run format:check).
rationale: One format for code and documents, LF line endings.
